headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Upstash documentation spans 1,809 crawled pages across a multi-project topology with 100% crawl coverage. The site suffers from 45 confirmed broken internal links, all within user-facing docs (0 repository links). Only 36.93% of pages display last-updated metadata, creating significant staleness risk. SEO/geo issues affect 20.59% of pages. Retrieval readiness scores 69.06/100 (moderate band), dragged down by 46.49% chunkability and 44.15% stale risk, though answerability (99.89%) and citationability (100%) are strong. API reference coverage is solid at 88.89% across 389 detected API pages, and example reliability estimates 84.6%.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Missing required doc layers
key_findings.business_consequence: Backfill concept/how-to/reference coverage for key capabilities.

priority_actions.title: Fix all 45 confirmed broken internal links across user-facing documentation
priority_actions.why_this_first: Broken links directly harm user trust, SEO ranking, and onboarding success; fixing 45 links is low-effort with immediate measurable impact on bounce rate and support tickets.

priority_actions.title: Add last-updated timestamps to the 63.07% of pages (approximately 1,141 pages) currently missing them
priority_actions.why_this_first: Freshness metadata directly improves user confidence, reduces support queries about outdated info, and boosts AI retrieval quality by signaling recency to LLMs and search engines.

priority_actions.title: Improve chunkability for the 53.51% of pages (approximately 968 pages) scoring poorly by refactoring long sections, adding semantic headings, and breaking dense blocks
priority_actions.why_this_first: Chunkability is the primary drag on retrieval readiness (69.06 overall); better chunking directly improves vector search precision, LLM answer quality, and user scanability across nearly 1,000 pages.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage (100.05%) with 1,809 pages successfully indexed from 1,898 discovered URLs
API reference coverage at 88.89% across 389 detected API pages with high detection confidence (85%)
Near-perfect answerability (99.89%) and citationability (100%) ensure AI retrieval can surface and attribute content reliably
risks: 45 confirmed broken internal links across user-facing docs damage trust, SEO authority, and user navigation
Only 36.93% of pages show last-updated dates, hiding content age from users and AI systems during retrieval
Chunkability at 46.49% means over half the corpus may fragment poorly for vector search and LLM context windows
SEO/geo issue rate of 20.59% (approximately 372 pages) risks organic discoverability and regional search performance
limitations: External audit cannot verify actual content accuracy, correctness of code examples, or whether API documentation matches live API behavior.
12 unverified links due to auth/rate-limit/server blocks mean true broken-link count may be underreported; manual investigation required.
Chunkability and stale-risk metrics are heuristic estimates; actual user comprehension and content freshness depend on domain-specific review.
automation_first: Deploy automated broken-link monitoring with daily scans across all 1,809 pages to catch the 45 current broken links and prevent new ones, reducing manual QA cycles and support escalations from navigation failures.

Implement CI/CD hooks to enforce last-updated timestamp injection on every commit, closing the 63.07% freshness gap (1,141 pages) and ensuring all future content carries recency signals for users and AI systems without manual tagging.

Add pre-commit linters to flag pages with poor chunkability (long sections >800 words, missing H2/H3 structure) targeting the 968 pages below threshold, preventing new low-chunkability content and guiding authors toward retrieval-optimized structure at creation time.
